This is the field the ranking itself is built on, and it is the same idea the Department of Education uses to sort international enrolments: "Enrolments are allocated to sectors based on their course level within the Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF).". Its five sectors are higher education, vocational education and training, schools, English language intensive courses for overseas students and non-award, so a three-part package of English, then a diploma, then a degree puts the degree in COE1, the diploma in COE2 and the English course here.
value_definition: A short descriptive string naming a course level. Levels are aligned to the Australian Qualifications Framework and roll up to five sectors, with courses outside the framework treated as non-award and English language courses treated as ELICOS whatever their level.
limitation: A level is not an outcome and not a duration. "Data is initially uploaded into PRISMS by education providers when an enrolment is offered to a prospective student before a visa is granted.", so the third-ranked level can belong to a student who never arrived, and nothing in the column says how long that course ran or whether the qualification was awarded. The block is filled for primary applicants only, so an empty value on a student visa row can mean the person is a partner or child included on someone else's application rather than that no enrolment existed.
rationale: The Department of Education's explanatory notes set out how course level maps to a sector under the Australian Qualifications Framework and list the five sectors PRISMS covers, which is the classification the text in this column comes from.
evidence_quote: Enrolments are allocated to sectors based on their course level within the Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF).
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's line about a course level from the CoE with the third highest course level and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so it never named the classification or explained the ranking.

value_source: Australian Government, business.gov.au, Register for an Australian business number (ABN)
variable_description: The education provider's Australian Business Number for the applicant's third-highest Confirmation of Enrolment, stored as hashed text. It sits on the 2000 to 2023 visa application extract, and the custodian's entire description for it is the parenthetical note that the variable has been hashed, so the meaning comes from the name: "An ABN is a unique 11-digit number that identifies your business to the government, other businesses and the public." (business.gov.au). Three vintages of the same fact sit in this dataset under three names, this one plus COE3_ABN_HASH_TRUNC on the 2000 to 2021 extract and COE3_PRVDR_ABN_TX_HASH_TRUNC on the extracts that run to 2025. It is empty unless the application carried three or more CoEs, so a filled value marks an unusually layered study package.
value_definition: An eleven-digit Australian Business Number carried as a text field and hashed, so the stored value is an opaque string of fixed length. The underlying classification is the Australian Business Register's ABN.
limitation: Values are not comparable across the three extracts. A hash produced for one extract is not guaranteed to equal the hash of the same ABN in another, so joining this column to COE3_ABN_HASH_TRUNC or COE3_PRVDR_ABN_TX_HASH_TRUNC is not a supported operation, and a provider that changes its ABN after a restructure looks like a different provider on either side of the change.
rationale: business.gov.au defines the ABN and what it identifies, which is the only way to attach a meaning to a column whose custodian description says nothing but that the field was hashed.
evidence_quote: An ABN is a unique 11-digit number that identifies your business to the government, other businesses and the public.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's bare note that the variable has been hashed as its whole description, with the generic no-value-list sentence printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so the page said nothing at all about what the field holds.

value_domain: Education provider ABN (hashed and truncated text)
value_source: Australian Government, business.gov.au, Register for an Australian business number (ABN)
variable_description: The education provider's Australian Business Number for the applicant's third-highest Confirmation of Enrolment, hashed and truncated. The column sits on the visa application extracts that run to 2025. "An ABN is a unique 11-digit number that identifies your business to the government, other businesses and the public." (business.gov.au), and truncating the hash trades a small chance of collision for a shorter key. The custodian's note that the value is for primary applicants only and comes from ICSE or IRIS names the departmental systems the value was drawn from, which is why it is missing on rows for family members. Set against the COE1 and COE2 columns on the same row, it says how many distinct businesses a three-course package was spread across.
value_definition: An eleven-digit Australian Business Number hashed and then cut to a fixed number of characters, giving an opaque short key. The underlying classification is the Australian Business Register's ABN.
limitation: A truncated hash can collide, so two different providers can share a value, and a group built on this column is a group of ABNs that hash alike rather than a group of businesses. It is also not the enrolling campus: an entity with sites in several states appears here once, and COE3_PRVDR_REG_STATE_CD is what carries location.
rationale: business.gov.au defines the ABN and what it identifies, which fixes the unit of this column as the provider's legal entity; the truncation and hashing are de-identification applied before the column reaches the asset.
evidence_quote: An ABN is a unique 11-digit number that identifies your business to the government, other businesses and the public.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's line about a provider ABN from the CoE with the third highest course level and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said what an ABN is or what truncating a hash costs the reader.

value_source: Department of Education, PRISMS frequently asked questions
variable_description: The education provider code on the applicant's third-highest Confirmation of Enrolment. "A CoE is an official document issued by a provider registered on the Commonwealth Register of Institutions and Courses for Overseas Students (CRICOS)." (Department of Education), so a value here means the college or university was on CRICOS and cleared to enrol overseas students at the time. It is the finer of the two provider identifiers in the block: COE3_PRVDR_ABN_TX_HASH_TRUNC gives the legal entity, while this code gives the registered provider that issued the CoE. The three CoE blocks on a row are ranked by course level, not by date, so this is the applicant's third highest course rather than their third course in time. It exists only for applicants with three or more CoEs, so it is the sparsest provider code on the row and is not a basis for a provider-level count.
value_definition: A provider identifier from the Commonwealth Register of Institutions and Courses for Overseas Students, carried through the Provider Registration and International Student Management System that issues Confirmations of Enrolment.
limitation: A provider code is not a campus and not a teaching location. A registered provider can deliver at several sites and can have its registration changed or cancelled, so a third-ranked code that disappears between two applications is a registration event rather than a student outcome, and the column cannot say where the student actually studied.
rationale: The Department of Education states that a CoE is issued by a CRICOS-registered provider, which is what makes this code a registration identifier rather than an ordinary organisation code.
evidence_quote: A CoE is an official document issued by a provider registered on the Commonwealth Register of Institutions and Courses for Overseas Students (CRICOS).
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's line about a provider code from the CoE with the third highest course level and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation.

value_domain: State or territory of the education provider on the third Confirmation of Enrolment
value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, PLIDA data and legislation; ABS Australian Statistical Geography Standard, Australia and State/Territory
variable_description: The state or territory where the education provider on the student's third-ranked Confirmation of Enrolment is registered. The visa application file holds three enrolment slots ranked by course level, so COE1_* is the highest course level, COE2_* the second and this the third. ABS describes the Home Affairs feed this comes from as carrying "data on educational studies for student visas", which is exactly this block of columns. It is recorded for primary applicants only, so a dependant travelling on a student visa has nothing here.

The ABS standard for the same concept uses one-digit codes 1 to 8 for the states and territories with 9 for Other Territories; whether Home Affairs codes to that order is not stated in the item list, so the mapping has to be read off the data.

The code also locates the provider's registration, not the student: someone studying at an interstate campus of a nationally registered provider counts to the provider's jurisdiction, and someone who never commenced the course still carries the code.
rationale: The ABS PLIDA page confirms that the Home Affairs visa feed carries educational study detail for student visas, which is what the COE block is, and the ABS geography standard supplies the state and territory concept behind the code.
evidence_quote: Information on visa types, start & end dates, & data on educational studies for student visas & working arrangements for skilled migration visas.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed only the custodian's wording about the third highest course level, with the generic sentence about no published value list printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it never said what a Confirmation of Enrolment is, why there are three of them, or that a blank means no third enrolment.

variable_description: The word label for the applicant's IELTS result, such as competent or good, rather than the number. IELTS reports on a nine-band scale with a label for each band: Band 9 is "Expert" and Band 0 is "Did not attempt the test". IELTS_OVRL on the same row carries the score the label came from, so the two are one result expressed twice. It is populated only for applicants who sat IELTS.
value_definition: A word label drawn from the IELTS nine-band descriptor set, one label per band from Band 1 to Band 9 plus a state for a test not attempted. It reports a sat test result, not a self-assessment of English.
limitation: A blank does not mean poor English. Applicants who took PTE Academic, TOEFL, Cambridge or OET, applicants exempt from the English requirement, and applicants on visas that never required a test are all blank, so restricting to non-blank rows selects a particular slice of the skilled and student programmes rather than the good English speakers.
rationale: IELTS publishes the band scale and the descriptor label attached to each band, which is what this column carries.
evidence_quote: Did not attempt the test
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's four-word description, 'English capability (IELTS) proficiency', with the generic no-value-list sentence used as both definition and limitation, so a reader could not tell it was a band label rather than a score, nor why it was missing for most people.

value_source: IELTS, IELTS scoring in detail
variable_description: The applicant's overall IELTS band score, the single number formed from the four skill bands. IELTS reports in half-band steps on a nine-band scale, so the value sits on 0, 0.5, 1.0 and so on rather than varying continuously. English requirements and points for skilled visas were set against this number, which makes it the field to use when reconstructing whether an applicant cleared a threshold. IELTS_ENGLISH_PROF is the word label for the same result.
value_definition: A number from 0 to 9 in half-band steps, formed by averaging the listening, reading, writing and speaking bands and rounding to a half or whole band. The four component bands are not carried separately in this table, so the composition of the score is lost.
limitation: It is not comparable with a score from another English test, and it carries no test date, so a score attached to a 2015 application may come from a test sat years earlier and a person who applies twice can show two different numbers with no way to order them. It also measures English at test time, not English after settlement.
rationale: IELTS publishes the band scale, the half-band reporting and the way the overall score is formed from the four sections, which is the shape of this column.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'English capability (IELTS) score' and the generic sentence about no finite value list twice over, so it never said the score runs 0 to 9 in half bands, that it is an average of four sections, or that no test date comes with it.

value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, PLIDA data and legislation
variable_description: A flag marking a skilled visa nomination made under a labour agreement rather than under the standard employer nomination rules. A labour agreement is a negotiated arrangement between the Commonwealth and an employer, industry or region that permits sponsorship in occupations or on terms the ordinary programme does not allow, so the flag separates a concessional pathway from the mainstream one. ABS describes this collection as holding "working arrangements for skilled migration visas", and this is one of those working arrangements.
value_definition: A two-state flag attached to the nomination, set where the nominated position sits under a labour agreement and otherwise not set. It describes the nomination, not the person nominated.
limitation: It does not name the agreement or the concession used, so a designated area migration agreement, a company-specific agreement and an industry agreement are indistinguishable. It also cannot tell you a visa followed, because a nominated position can lapse or be withdrawn with the flag still set.
rationale: The ABS PLIDA page confirms this Home Affairs feed carries the working arrangements attached to skilled migration visas, which is the block of nomination and sponsorship columns this flag belongs to.
evidence_quote: Information on visa types, start & end dates, & data on educational studies for student visas & working arrangements for skilled migration visas.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed only the custodian's sentence about identifying visas under a labour agreement, with the generic no-value-list line as both definition and limitation, so it never explained what a labour agreement is or that the flag attaches to a nomination rather than to a grant.

value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, PLIDA data and legislation
variable_description: The day the department approved the employer's nomination of a position, which is a separate decision from granting the visa. An employer-sponsored skilled visa runs in stages: a sponsor is approved, a position is nominated (NM_LODGED_DT), the nomination is approved, and only then is a visa granted. This column dates the third stage, and the gap between it and the lodgement date is nomination processing time.
value_definition: A calendar date with an open domain, running over the collection's coverage from 2000 onward. It is populated only for applications that went through an employer or government nomination, which is a minority of the file.
limitation: A blank carries three different meanings that the column cannot separate: the visa needed no nomination, the nomination was refused or withdrawn, or it was still undecided at the extract. rationale: The ABS PLIDA page establishes that this Home Affairs feed carries the working arrangements attached to skilled migration visas, which is the nomination sequence this date sits inside.
evidence_quote: Information on visa types, start & end dates, & data on educational studies for student visas & working arrangements for skilled migration visas.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Approval date of the nominated application' with the generic sentence about no finite value list repeated as definition and limitation, so it never placed the date in the sponsor-nominate-grant sequence or warned what a blank means.

value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, PLIDA data and legislation
variable_description: The identifier for the employer's nomination, shared by everyone on it, so a primary applicant and their family all carry the same value. It is the key that ties a family's visa applications to one nominated position, and the key that lets several nominations by the same sponsor be counted. VA_CASE_ID is the parallel identifier for the visa application itself, and SP_CLIENT_ID identifies the sponsor behind the nomination.
value_definition: An opaque identifier with no meaning in its digits. It identifies a nomination event, not a person, not an employer and not a job.
limitation: Counting distinct values does not count jobs or workers. The same position renominated when a visa expires gets a fresh identifier, an employer with several vacancies in one occupation lodges several nominations, and a nomination that was never used still has an identifier, so the count is of administrative events only.
rationale: The ABS PLIDA page confirms this collection carries the skilled visa working arrangements, and the identifier's behaviour across primary and secondary applicants is stated in the custodian's own item list.
evidence_quote: Information on visa types, start & end dates, & data on educational studies for student visas & working arrangements for skilled migration visas.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's note that secondary applicants share the primary's identifier, with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said what a nomination is or why counting the identifier is not counting jobs.

value_domain: State or territory of the nominated position
value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Australia and State/Territory
variable_description: The state or territory of the nominated position on an employer-sponsored skilled visa. A secondary applicant inherits the primary applicant's nomination, so a partner and children on the same case all carry the primary's work location. It is the closest thing the visa file has to an intended place of work, and it is fixed at nomination rather than observed after arrival. ABS says of the same geographic concept that "In general, the total area of each State and Territory, including their offshore islands, is used for statistical purposes as a separate geographic area in the ASGS."
value_definition: A single code for one Australian state or territory. The ABS standard for the concept uses one-digit codes 1 through 8 with 9 for Other Territories; the item list does not say whether Home Affairs follows that order, so the codes must be checked against known cases.
limitation: It is not where the person lived or worked. Nothing in the visa stops a holder moving interstate after arrival, a state-nominated regional visa records the nominating jurisdiction rather than the workplace, and the field is blank for every visa granted without a nomination, which is most of the file.
rationale: The ABS geography standard defines the state and territory concept and publishes the one-digit code set that any Australian jurisdiction code of this shape is measured against.
evidence_quote: In general, the total area of each State and Territory, including their offshore islands, is used for statistical purposes as a separate geographic area in the ASGS.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's sentence about the nominated position location with the generic no-value-list line as both definition and limitation, so it never gave a candidate code set and never warned that the location is an intention rather than an observed workplace.

value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, PLIDA data and legislation
variable_description: The day the employer lodged the nomination of a position for a skilled visa. The custodian's own text for this column is a mistake: it repeats the NM_CASE_ID description about secondary applicants and does not describe a date at all, so the column name and the date_time tag are the evidence for what it holds. Read against NM_APPRVL_DT it gives nomination processing time, and against VA_LODGED_DT it says whether the employer or the applicant moved first.
value_definition: A calendar date marking the start of the nomination stage, so on a well-formed row it is the earliest of the nomination dates and sits at or before NM_APPRVL_DT. It exists only where the visa pathway required an employer or government nomination, and unlike the approval date it is present for nominations that were refused or withdrawn as well as approved ones.
limitation: The identification of this column rests on its name rather than on documentation, so check it against NM_APPRVL_DT before use: a lodgement date sitting after its own approval date would show the mapping is wrong. Beyond that, a lodged nomination is not labour demand met, because a nomination later withdrawn looks identical here to one that produced a worker.
rationale: No fetchable page documents this column, and the custodian's own description for it is a copy of another variable's text, so the reading rests on the column name and its neighbours rather than on a source.
supersedes_rationale: The entry printed the custodian's broken sentence, 'The date on which the nomination identifier is the same as the primary applicants', with the generic no-value-list line as definition and limitation, so the page asserted something that is not a description of a date and gave no warning that the metadata is wrong.

value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, ANZSCO classification structure, 2022
variable_description: The occupation code for the position an employer nominated, recorded in whichever occupation classification was current at the time. ASCO described the Australian labour market to 2005 and ANZSCO from 2006, so a nomination from 2003 and one from 2015 carry codes from different classifications in the same column. NM_OCPTN_TYPE_CD says which edition applies and NM_OCPTN_FULL_DS gives the words. ABS states that "Occupations are subdivisions of the unit groups and are denoted by 6-digit codes (the relevant unit group code plus an additional two digits)."
value_definition: A numeric occupation code. ANZSCO occupations are six digits sitting under a four-digit unit group, a three-digit minor group, a two-digit sub-major group and a one-digit major group; ASCO is structured differently, so code length alone does not identify the edition.
limitation: Pooling the column across years silently mixes two classifications, and the same number can name different occupations in each, so a long time series of nominated occupations built without conversion is wrong rather than noisy. The code also describes the position the employer nominated, not the work the person did after arrival.
rationale: The ABS classification structure page gives the exact code geometry for ANZSCO occupations, which is the classification most of this column uses, and the ABS occupation classification history establishes the ASCO to ANZSCO boundary.
evidence_quote: Occupations are subdivisions of the unit groups and are denoted by 6-digit codes (the relevant unit group code plus an additional two digits).
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed only the custodian's sentence naming ASCO or ANZSCO, with the generic no-value-list line as both definition and limitation, so it never gave the code geometry nor warned that pooling across editions breaks the series.

value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, Previous occupation classifications
variable_description: The occupation title of the nominated position, written out rather than coded. It is the label attached to NM_OCPTN_CD, so it comes from ASCO for older nominations and ANZSCO for later ones: ABS records that "The Australian and New Zealand Standard Classification of Occupations replaced ASCO. ANZSCO described the labour markets of Australia and New Zealand from 2006 to 2024." Titles are the field to read a case with, and the code is the field to group on.
value_definition: Text carrying the classification's own occupation title. The vocabulary is closed within an edition, being the titles of the classification in force, but not closed across editions.
limitation: It is not a job title from an employment contract. An employer nominates against the nearest available classification title, so a person whose contract says data scientist can appear under an older analyst title, and searching this column for a modern job name will miss them entirely.
rationale: The ABS page on previous occupation classifications states which classification was in use over which period, which is what decides the wording this column carries in any given year.
evidence_quote: The Australian and New Zealand Standard Classification of Occupations replaced ASCO. ANZSCO described the labour markets of Australia and New Zealand from 2006 to 2024.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's phrase 'the full nominated occupation description' with the generic no-value-list line twice over, so it never said the titles come from a classification whose wording changes between editions.

value_domain: Occupation classification edition code for the nominated occupation
value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, Previous occupation classifications
variable_description: The code saying which occupation classification edition NM_OCPTN_CD was recorded in, an ASCO edition or an ANZSCO one. It is the key that makes the nominated occupation code interpretable across a file spanning three decades. ABS records that ASCO "described the Australian labour market from 1986 to 2005" and that ANZSCO "described the labour markets of Australia and New Zealand from 2006 to 2024". It is recorded for primary applicants only.
value_definition: A short code naming a classification and its edition. The candidate set is small, covering the ASCO editions and the ANZSCO editions and revisions, but the department's own labels for them are not published in the item list.
limitation: A populated occupation code with a missing edition code is unusable, because the number cannot be resolved to an occupation at all, and this is the failure the column exists to prevent rather than to report. The code will also not carry OSCA, which replaced ANZSCO from December 2024, for anything recorded before the department switched.
rationale: The ABS page on previous occupation classifications names both classifications and the years each described the labour market, which is precisely what this edition code distinguishes.
evidence_quote: The Australian Standard Classification of Occupations was the first occupation classification based on skill level and skill specialisation. It described the Australian labour market from 1986 to 2005.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording about ASCO or ANZSCO codes for primary applicants, with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it never explained that the edition code is what rescues the occupation code from ambiguity.

value_domain: Nominated base salary in Australian dollars
value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, PLIDA data and legislation
variable_description: The base salary the employer offered for the nominated position, in Australian dollars. It is the guaranteed annual earnings figure the department assessed the nomination against, so it is the field a skilled migration income threshold bites on. NM_TOTAL_RMNRTN_AM on the same row is the wider figure that adds non-salary components, and the difference between the two is the size of the package beyond salary.
value_definition: An annual amount in nominal Australian dollars at the date of nomination, neither indexed nor deflated. It records an offer written on a nomination, not a payment.
limitation: It is not earnings. The person may never take the position, may be paid more or less, or may work part of the year, and the tax and payroll products in PLIDA carry what was actually paid. Comparing the amount across two decades without deflating also mixes 2001 and 2024 dollars, which will read as real wage growth that is not there.
rationale: The ABS PLIDA page confirms this feed carries the working arrangements attached to skilled migration visas, which is the nomination block this salary sits in.
evidence_quote: Information on visa types, start & end dates, & data on educational studies for student visas & working arrangements for skilled migration visas.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's phrase about the base salary for visas with a nomination and the generic no-value-list line twice, so it never said the amount is an offer rather than earnings, nor that it is nominal dollars.

value_domain: Nominated total remuneration in Australian dollars
value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, PLIDA data and legislation
variable_description: The total remuneration offered for the nominated position, being base salary plus other agreed money benefits. It sits beside NM_SALARY_AM, so subtracting one from the other isolates the non-salary part of the package. Where only one of the pair is populated, the collection is carrying whatever the nomination form of that year asked for.
value_definition: An annual amount in nominal Australian dollars covering the whole remuneration package on the nomination. It is a single number with no breakdown of its components.

It also cannot be assumed to be defined identically across the whole period, because the nomination forms it is drawn from were redesigned several times.
rationale: The ABS PLIDA page establishes that the Home Affairs visa feed carries skilled visa working arrangements, of which the nominated remuneration is one.
evidence_quote: Information on visa types, start & end dates, & data on educational studies for student visas & working arrangements for skilled migration visas.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's phrase about the remuneration salary for visas with a nomination, with the generic no-value-list line as both definition and limitation, so it never distinguished total remuneration from base salary or warned the composition is not recoverable.

variable_description: The sponsoring employer's Australian Business Number, hashed and truncated, on the 2000 to 2021 version of the visa application file. The Australian Business Register defines the underlying identifier: "The Australian Business Number (ABN) is a unique 11 digit identifier issued to all entities registered in the Australian Business Register (ABR)." It is populated only where the visa involved a sponsorship, so it is empty for family, student and visitor visas. evidence_quote: The Australian Business Number (ABN) is a unique 11 digit identifier issued to all entities registered in the Australian Business Register (ABR).
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's terse note about sponsors' ABNs in ICSE, with the generic sentence about no finite value list used as both value definition and limitation, so it never said what an ABN is, that the value is hashed beyond recovery, or that it identifies an entity rather than an employer.

variable_description: The sponsoring employer's ABN on the 2000 to 2023 version of the visa application file, held as text and hashed before release. evidence_quote: The Australian Business Number (ABN) is a unique 11 digit identifier issued to all entities registered in the Australian Business Register (ABR).
supersedes_rationale: The entry rendered as the bare parenthetical '(note: variable has been hashed)' with the generic no-value-list line as definition and limitation, so the page said nothing at all about whose ABN it is or which file vintage it belongs to.

value_source: Australian Business Register, ABN format
variable_description: The sponsoring employer's ABN, hashed and truncated, on the long 1990 to 2025 version of the visa application file. supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's fragment about sponsors' ABNs for visa holders with a sponsorship, with the generic no-value-list line printed twice, so it never explained the identifier, the hashing, or that a blank often means an individual sponsor.

value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, PLIDA data and legislation
variable_description: The department's own identifier for the sponsor, treating the sponsoring party as a client of the department rather than as a business. Every approved sponsor has one, whether a company, a partnership or an individual, so it covers the cases where no ABN exists. Sponsor and nomination are different objects: this says who sponsored, and NM_CASE_ID says which position they nominated.
value_definition: An opaque departmental identifier with no structure to read. It identifies a sponsorship client record, and one client record can carry many nominations over many years.
limitation: It is not stable against corporate change. A restructure, a change of legal entity or a fresh sponsorship application can create a second client record for what a reader would call the same employer, so counting distinct values overstates the number of sponsors and understates how long each sponsored for.
rationale: The ABS PLIDA page establishes that the Home Affairs visa feed carries the sponsorship arrangements behind skilled visas, which is the record this identifier keys.
evidence_quote: Information on visa types, start & end dates, & data on educational studies for student visas & working arrangements for skilled migration visas.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the two-word description 'Sponsors Identifier' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it never distinguished the sponsor from the nomination or warned that the identifier is not stable across corporate change.

value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, PLIDA data and legislation
variable_description: A flag marking that the sponsor was an individual person rather than a business. It matters because the sponsor identifiers behave differently in the two cases: an individual sponsor has no ABN, so the ABN columns are empty and SP_CLIENT_ID is the only handle on who they were. It sits on the skilled side of the file, so it is not the same idea as the sponsor of a family visa.
value_definition: A two-state flag on the sponsorship record distinguishing an individual sponsor from a business sponsor. It describes the sponsoring party, not the visa applicant.
limitation: It does not identify the individual and does not link them to a person record, so a sponsor cannot be followed as a person through PLIDA. And because the flag only exists where a sponsorship exists, a blank means no sponsorship far more often than it means a business sponsor.
rationale: The ABS PLIDA page confirms the visa feed carries the sponsorship arrangements for skilled visas, which is the record this flag qualifies.
evidence_quote: Information on visa types, start & end dates, & data on educational studies for student visas & working arrangements for skilled migration visas.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's typo-ridden sentence about visas sponsored by an individual, with the generic no-value-list line as both definition and limitation, so it never said why the distinction matters for the ABN columns or what a blank means.

value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, Australian and New Zealand Standard Industrial Classification (ANZSIC)
variable_description: The industry of the sponsoring employer, written out in words and recorded for primary applicants only. It is the closest the visa file comes to saying which sector a sponsored migrant entered. ABS defines the national standard for the concept: the Australian and New Zealand Standard Industrial Classification "has been developed for use in the compilation and analysis of industry statistics in Australia and New Zealand", and it runs division, subdivision, group and class.
value_definition: A text industry label attached to the sponsor. The item list does not say whether the label is ANZSIC and, if so, at which level of the division to class hierarchy, so the granularity has to be read off the values themselves.
limitation: It describes the sponsor, not the job. A cook sponsored by a labour hire company falls under administrative services rather than accommodation and food services, a person who changes employer after arrival keeps the original sponsor's industry on this row, and secondary applicants are blank even when they go on to work.
rationale: ABS publishes the standard industry classification against which any Australian industry label of this kind is measured, and states its purpose and hierarchy.
evidence_quote: The Australian and New Zealand Standard Industrial Classification (ANZSIC) has been developed for use in the compilation and analysis of industry statistics in Australia and New Zealand.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's sentence about the sponsor's industry for primary applicants with the generic no-value-list line repeated as definition and limitation, so it never named a classification or warned that a labour hire sponsor puts the worker in the wrong sector.

value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, PLIDA data and legislation
variable_description: The person key that links a visa record to the same person's records elsewhere in PLIDA. It appears on both the visa application and the visa grant tables, which is what lets an application be followed through to its grant and then out to tax, education and health products. ABS describes the Home Affairs client feed as covering "Australian-born citizens, temporary & permanent migrants", so the key is not confined to migrants. In fplida it names a synthetic person generated to behave like the real key.
value_definition: An opaque person-level key with no readable structure. A person can carry many rows, one for each visa application or grant, so the key is the unit of analysis and the row is not.
limitation: It is not a family, a household or an application. A primary applicant and their partner have different person keys on the same VA_CASE_ID, so counting keys counts people and counting rows counts neither people nor visas. A person who did not link to the spine cannot be followed out of the visa file at all, and that non-linkage is not flagged here.
rationale: The ABS PLIDA page describes the Home Affairs client information feed and its population, which is the population this person key indexes.
evidence_quote: Client information on Australian-born citizens, temporary & permanent migrants.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Person Identifier' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed as both value definition and limitation, so it never said the key spans both visa tables, nor that a row is a visa event rather than a person.

value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, PLIDA data and legislation
variable_description: The visa application number on the grant record, hashed by ABS, which is the key back from a grant to the application that produced it. The TR_ prefix marks a column drawn from the department's Travel and Immigration Processing System, the system ABS names when describing the movement records it takes from Home Affairs: "All overseas movement records on Home Affairs' Travel & Immigration Processing System." The grant table has only twelve columns, so this identifier is how the richer application detail is attached to a grant.
value_definition: A hashed application number. One application identifier can cover several people and, where a case produced more than one decision, several grant rows.
limitation: It cannot be assumed to match VA_CASE_ID on the application table, because the two sides come from different source systems and different hashing. Where a grant has no matching application, the likeliest reason is that the grant predates the application file's coverage rather than that a visa was granted without an application.
rationale: The ABS PLIDA page names the Travel and Immigration Processing System as the Home Affairs source system the TR_ columns are drawn from, and confirms this collection holds visa information from 2000.
evidence_quote: All overseas movement records on Home Affairs' Travel & Immigration Processing System.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'Visa application number (ABS hashed)' with the generic no-value-list line as both definition and limitation, so it never said what the identifier joins to, nor that it need not match the application table's own case identifier.

value_domain: Country of citizenship of the visa holder
value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, Standard Australian Classification of Countries (SACC)
variable_description: The country the visa holder was a citizen of when the visa was granted. It is citizenship at grant, not country of birth and not current nationality. ABS's standard for the concept is SACC, which "provides guidelines for consistent collection, aggregation and dissemination of statistics by country" and uses four-digit country codes inside a nine-group hierarchy; the item list does not say whether Home Affairs codes to SACC or to its own passport-oriented list.
value_definition: A country code whose width and classification are not published here, so the code list has to be read from the data. SACC gives four digits; passport-driven systems commonly use three-letter or three-digit ISO codes instead.
limitation: It is not country of birth and not the country the person travelled from. A person who naturalised in a third country before applying shows that later citizenship, dual nationals appear under one country only, and stateless and refugee applicants can carry a code that names a status rather than a country.
rationale: ABS publishes the national standard for classifying countries in Australian statistics, which is the yardstick for any country code in a PLIDA product.
evidence_quote: The Standard Australian Classification of Countries (SACC) provides guidelines for consistent collection, aggregation and dissemination of statistics by country.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's phrase about the citizenship country of the visa holder in TRIPS, with the generic sentence about no finite value list used twice, so it never named a candidate classification or separated citizenship from birthplace.

value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, PLIDA data and legislation
variable_description: The visa holder's marital status as most recently recorded before the visa was granted. It is a status at a point in time held on the department's TRIPS record, so it moves when the department updates its file, not when the person's circumstances change. Read it alongside TR_PRIMARY_FLAG, which says whether the person applied in their own right or as a family member of someone who did.
value_definition: A short text status label. Home Affairs categories here are administrative, so they need not line up with the registered marital status and social marital status categories ABS uses in the Census.
limitation: It cannot be used to build a couple, because it names no partner and carries no relationship identifier. The value can also be years stale relative to the grant date, de facto and married partners are not guaranteed to be handled consistently across the period, and a partner visa holder's status at grant says nothing about whether the relationship lasted.
rationale: No fetchable page documents the department's marital status categories, so the reading rests on the column name, the TRIPS attribution in the custodian's own note, and the ABS description of the collection.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's line about the most recent marital status to the visa grant date, with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it never warned the status can be stale or that it will not reconstruct couples.

value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, PLIDA data and legislation
variable_description: The day the person was granted Australian citizenship, carried on their visa grant record. ABS lists the Home Affairs feed as "Visa information & Citizenship grants" from 2000, so citizenship sits inside this collection rather than in a product of its own. The date turns the visa file into a settlement pathway: it closes the visa sequence for those who naturalise, and the interval from TR_VISA_GRANT_DT to this date is time from that visa to citizenship.
value_definition: A calendar date, populated only for people granted citizenship. It records a grant, which for citizenship by conferral is a ministerial decision taking effect on a stated day.
limitation: A blank is not evidence the person is not a citizen. Citizenship by descent and citizenship by birth in Australia are not grants, so an Australian-born person in the file has no date at all, and anyone naturalising after the extract has none yet. The date is also not an arrival, a residence marker or a permanent residence date.
rationale: The ABS PLIDA page names citizenship grants explicitly as part of this Home Affairs feed and gives its start year, which is what makes this column part of the visa collection rather than an orphan.
evidence_quote: Information on visa types, start & end dates, & data on educational studies for student visas & working arrangements for skilled migration visas.
supersedes_rationale: The entry printed the custodian's sentence about the date the person was granted Australian citizenship in TRIPS, with the generic no-value-list line twice, so it never explained why a blank is common or that only conferral shows up here.

value_domain: Primary or secondary applicant indicator on the grant
value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24
variable_description: A flag saying whether the person was the primary applicant on the granted visa or a secondary applicant such as a partner or child. It separates the person whose skills, English and occupation were assessed from the family members who came with them. ABS carries the same idea in its migration statistics as "Visa applicant type (primary or secondary applicant - available from Sep quarter 2011)". Almost every skills column in this collection is populated for primary applicants only, so the flag predicts which rows are rich and which are sparse.
value_definition: A single character on the grant record, Y for primary and N for secondary. VA_PRIMARY_FL is the same concept on the application table.
limitation: It does not say what the relationship was, so a spouse, a de facto partner and a dependent child are indistinguishable and no family can be assembled from it. Restricting an analysis to primary applicants also removes most women who arrived on skilled visas, which biases any labour market comparison built that way.
rationale: ABS names primary and secondary applicant as a Home Affairs visa data item in its overseas migration methodology, which is the same administrative distinction this flag records.
evidence_quote: Visa applicant type (primary or secondary applicant - available from Sep quarter 2011)
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's line about a flag indicating primary or secondary applicants in TRIPS, with the generic no-value-list sentence used as both definition and limitation, so it never said the flag drives the sparsity of the skills columns or that it cannot build a family.

value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, PLIDA data and legislation
variable_description: The number of days the visa permits the holder to stay in Australia. It is a permission expressed as a length rather than as a date, and it really describes temporary visas: a visitor visa permits a stay measured in months and a student visa one measured in years, while a permanent visa has no meaningful stay period. Read with TR_VISA_IN_EFFECT_UNTIL_DT it separates how long the visa lasts from how long any one stay inside it may be.
value_definition: A whole number of days attached to the visa grant. On a multiple-entry visa it is the length permitted for each stay, not the total time the visa may be used across entries.
limitation: It is not time spent in Australia. A holder can leave early, never arrive at all, or on a multiple-entry visa accumulate far more days in the country than the number shown; the traveller movement records are where actual presence lives. Very large or zero values on permanent visas should be read as not applicable rather than as real durations.
rationale: The ABS PLIDA page confirms this Home Affairs feed carries visa start and end dates and visa types, which is the block of duration fields this belongs to.
evidence_quote: Information on visa types, start & end dates, & data on educational studies for student visas & working arrangements for skilled migration visas.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's phrase about the period in days a visa holder can stay, with the generic no-value-list line as both value definition and limitation, so it never separated permitted stay from time actually spent, nor flagged the multiple-entry case.

value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, PLIDA data and legislation
variable_description: The day the department granted this visa, which opens the visa episode and anchors the whole grant record. ABS describes the collection as holding visa "start & end dates", and this is the start; TR_VISA_IN_EFFECT_UNTIL_DT closes the episode and TR_STAY_PERIOD_DD limits each stay inside it. A person with several rows has a visa history, and sorting on this date reconstructs it.
value_definition: A calendar date on the grant record, running from 2000 onward in this collection. Every granted visa carries one, which makes it the least sparse date in the file.
limitation: It is not an arrival date, and for a visa granted onshore it corresponds to no border crossing at all. It also does not mean the visa was used: a visitor visa granted and left to expire looks identical here to one that carried a person into the country, so grant counts are not entry counts.
rationale: The ABS PLIDA page states that this Home Affairs feed carries visa start and end dates from 2000, which is what this column and its partner end date are.
evidence_quote: Information on visa types, start & end dates, & data on educational studies for student visas & working arrangements for skilled migration visas.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the two-word description 'Visa grant date' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the grant date is not an arrival and that a grant need not have been used.

value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, PLIDA data and legislation
variable_description: The identifier of the granted visa itself, hashed by ABS, which distinguishes one grant from another for the same person. A person accumulates grants over time, a student visa then a graduate visa then a skilled visa, and this number is what keeps them apart. VA_VISA_GRANT_NR is the counterpart carried on the application table, which is how a grant is tied back to the application that produced it.
value_definition: A hashed grant number, unique to a single grant. It does not repeat across the family members on one application: each person's own grant carries its own number.
limitation: Counting distinct grant numbers is not counting migrants or arrivals. One person can hold several in a year, a bridging visa granted while another application is decided produces a number that represents no new entry, and a cancelled visa keeps its number, so grant counts overstate movement of people.
rationale: The ABS PLIDA page confirms the Home Affairs visa feed carries visa grants with their start and end dates, which is the record this identifier keys.
evidence_quote: Information on visa types, start & end dates, & data on educational studies for student visas & working arrangements for skilled migration visas.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Visa grant number (ABS hashed)' with the generic no-value-list line as both definition and limitation, so it never said the number is per person rather than per case, nor warned against reading grant counts as arrivals.

value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, PLIDA data and legislation
variable_description: The last day this visa is in effect, closing the episode that TR_VISA_GRANT_DT opened. ABS describes the collection as carrying visa "start & end dates", and this is the end. For a temporary visa it is the expiry; for a permanent visa it is generally the travel facility rather than the residence right that expires, so the date can pass while the person's permanent residence continues.
value_definition: A calendar date that may fall in the future relative to the extract, so a visa still running when the data were taken carries a date that has not yet happened.
limitation: It is not the day the visa actually ceased. Cancellation, a later visa taking effect and departure all end a visa's practical life earlier without this field being changed, so treating it as the end of lawful stay overstates how long temporary migrants held their visas.
rationale: The ABS PLIDA page states that the Home Affairs visa feed carries visa start and end dates, and this column is the end date on the grant record.
evidence_quote: Information on visa types, start & end dates, & data on educational studies for student visas & working arrangements for skilled migration visas.
supersedes_rationale: The entry printed the custodian's clause about the date until which the visa will be in effect, with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never distinguished a scheduled expiry from an actual cessation or explained the permanent visa case.

value_domain: Home Affairs visa subclass code on the grant
value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, Migrant settlement outcomes methodology, 2025
variable_description: The subclass code of the visa that was granted, covering permanent and temporary visas alike. Subclass is the finest level of the visa taxonomy, for example 500 for a student visa or 601 for an electronic travel authority, and everything else is built above it: ABS states that "Visa subclass (3-digit) information was aggregated into visa streams (highest-level grouping)". VISA_SUBCLASS_CD on the application table is the subclass sought, and the two can differ where a case was decided into another subclass.
value_definition: A three digit code identifying a visa subclass prescribed under the Migration Regulations 1994. The set is open over time, since subclasses are created and closed as the programme changes, so the codes present depend on the grant year.
limitation: A subclass is not a migration outcome, and an unfamiliar code is not automatically an error. The subclass set changed repeatedly over the collection's span, so a code that looks wrong is more often a subclass closed before you started looking than a data fault, and a closed subclass appearing in later years usually marks a grandfathered case rather than a live pathway. Check any unfamiliar code against the subclass list in force for that grant year before treating it as an error.
rationale: The ABS methodology states that visa subclass is a three digit code and is the level from which higher visa groupings are built, which is what this column carries.
evidence_quote: Visa subclass (3-digit) information was aggregated into visa streams (highest-level grouping).
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's line about subclass codes for permanent and temporary visas in TRIPS, with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it never gave the code width, the changing subclass set, or the risk of non-subclass fillers.

value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, PLIDA data and legislation
variable_description: The application identifier, shared by everyone included on the same visa application. It is the grouping key for a migrating family: a primary applicant and their dependants have different person keys but one case identifier. Counting distinct values counts applications and counting rows counts people on applications, which are different numbers. NM_CASE_ID is the parallel identifier for the employer's nomination where one exists.
value_definition: An opaque case identifier with no readable structure. One case can produce several grants, one for each person included on it.
limitation: It is not a person and not a household. People on one application need not live together after arrival, and a person who applies three times has three case identifiers, so it cannot deduplicate people. It also cannot be assumed to equal TR_APLCTN_ID on the grant table, which comes from a different system.
rationale: The ABS PLIDA page establishes that this Home Affairs feed carries visa applications alongside grants, which is what makes a case identifier meaningful across the two tables.
evidence_quote: Information on visa types, start & end dates, & data on educational studies for student visas & working arrangements for skilled migration visas.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's sentence about identifying the applicants on each application, with the generic no-value-list line twice, so it never said what counting the identifier counts or warned it need not match the grant table's key.

value_domain: Applicant location at lodgement (onshore, offshore, unknown)
value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, PLIDA data and legislation
variable_description: Where the applicant physically was when the application was lodged: in Australia, outside Australia, or unknown. The onshore against offshore split is one of the most useful facts in the file, because it separates people already in the country changing visa from people applying to come. Student to graduate to skilled sequences are onshore; most first visas are offshore.
value_definition: A one digit code with three states, given in the item list as in Australia = 3, outside Australia = 4 and unknown = 1. The codes are unordered and the gap at 2 carries no meaning.
limitation: It is not a residence measure and not a visa status. Someone lodging onshore may have arrived weeks earlier on a visitor visa, and unknown is a real category rather than an error, so dropping unknown rows will push the onshore share upward by an amount that varies by year.
rationale: The ABS PLIDA page confirms the collection carries Home Affairs visa applications, and the three codes come from the custodian's own item list text for this column.
evidence_quote: Information on visa types, start & end dates, & data on educational studies for student visas & working arrangements for skilled migration visas.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's sentence with the codes embedded in it and the generic no-value-list line as both value definition and limitation, which was self-contradictory: the description listed three codes while the definition claimed no value list existed.

value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, PLIDA data and legislation
variable_description: The day the visa application was lodged, which starts the application's clock. With VA_VISA_GRANT_NR and the grant table's TR_VISA_GRANT_DT it gives processing time, and with VA_CLNT_LOCN_CD it says whether the person waited inside the country or outside it. A lodgement with no matching grant is an application refused, withdrawn, or still on hand at the extract.
value_definition: A calendar date on the application record, present for every application regardless of outcome. It is the only date the file holds for applications that never produced a visa.
limitation: It does not fix a queue position. Processing priority in the skilled programme has depended on occupation, nomination and programme year rather than on lodgement order, so ranking applications by this date will not reproduce the order in which they were decided. It is also not a decision to migrate and not an arrival.
rationale: The ABS PLIDA page confirms the Home Affairs feed carries visa applications from 2000 with their dates, which is what this column records.
evidence_quote: Information on visa types, start & end dates, & data on educational studies for student visas & working arrangements for skilled migration visas.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's phrase about the date the visa application was lodged and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said this is the only date unsuccessful applications carry, nor that it does not fix processing order.

value_domain: Usual occupation code of the applicant (ASCO or ANZSCO)
value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, ANZSCO classification structure, 2022
variable_description: The applicant's own usual occupation code, which is what the person does rather than the position an employer nominated. The contrast with NM_OCPTN_CD is the point: this is the applicant's stated occupation and that is the employer's job. Like the nominated code it uses whichever classification was current, with VA_OCPTN_TYPE_CD naming the edition. ABS states that "The structure of ANZSCO has five hierarchical levels - major group, sub-major group, minor group, unit group and occupation."
value_definition: A numeric occupation code from the classification named in VA_OCPTN_TYPE_CD, six digits at the occupation level under ANZSCO and structured differently under ASCO.
limitation: It is a claim on a form, not a verified job. Skilled visa applicants have an incentive to state the occupation that scores, while visitor and family applicants have no reason to state anything precise, so the column's accuracy varies by visa type rather than being uniformly good or uniformly poor.
rationale: The ABS classification structure page gives the hierarchy and code geometry of the classification this column is coded to for most of its span.
evidence_quote: The structure of ANZSCO has five hierarchical levels - major group, sub-major group, minor group, unit group and occupation.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's line about the usual occupation code in ASCO or ANZSCO with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so it never separated the applicant's occupation from the nominated one or warned about self-reporting incentives.

value_domain: Usual occupation title of the applicant
value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, ANZSCO classification structure, 2022
variable_description: The applicant's own usual occupation written out in words rather than coded. It is the readable label for VA_OCPTN_CD and comes from the same classification edition, so use it to read a case and use the code to group. NM_OCPTN_FULL_DS is the equivalent title for the employer's nominated position, and the two can differ on the same row.
value_definition: Text carrying an occupation title from the classification in force at lodgement. It is a closed classification title, not a free-text job description written by the applicant.
limitation: It cannot be matched to the job titles employers report in the payroll and tax products, because those are not coded to any classification. Text matching between the two will fail on synonyms and will quietly produce a biased subset rather than an obvious error.
rationale: The ABS classification structure page describes the occupation level whose titles this column carries.
evidence_quote: The structure of ANZSCO has five hierarchical levels - major group, sub-major group, minor group, unit group and occupation.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Full occupation description' with the generic no-value-list line printed as both value definition and limitation, so it never said the words come from a classification or warned against matching them to employer-reported titles.

value_domain: Occupation classification edition code for the applicant's occupation
value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, Previous occupation classifications
variable_description: The code naming which occupation classification edition VA_OCPTN_CD uses, ASCO or ANZSCO. It is the companion to the applicant's own occupation code, exactly as NM_OCPTN_TYPE_CD is to the nominated one, and the two need not agree on a row where application and nomination were recorded years apart. ABS records that "The Australian and New Zealand Standard Classification of Occupations replaced ASCO. ANZSCO described the labour markets of Australia and New Zealand from 2006 to 2024."
value_definition: A short code naming a classification and edition. The values are few and the boundary between them falls around the middle of the 2000s, when ANZSCO came into use.
limitation: It does not always carry the ANZSCO version or revision, so two records both coded as ANZSCO can sit on different revisions with different occupation lists. It also will not flag a record where the department kept coding to the older edition after a new one was published, which is the case most likely to mislead.
rationale: The ABS page on previous occupation classifications names both classifications and the periods each covered, which is the distinction this edition code makes.
evidence_quote: The Australian and New Zealand Standard Classification of Occupations replaced ASCO. ANZSCO described the labour markets of Australia and New Zealand from 2006 to 2024.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's phrase about the ASCO or ANZSCO edition code, with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it never gave the period each classification covered nor the revision problem inside ANZSCO.

value_domain: Primary or secondary applicant indicator on the application
value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24
variable_description: A flag on the application saying whether this person was the primary applicant or a secondary applicant. It is the application-side twin of TR_PRIMARY_FLAG on the grant table, and it is the field that explains sparsity elsewhere: occupation, English, nomination and sponsor industry columns in this table are recorded for primary applicants only. ABS carries the same item as "Visa applicant type (primary or secondary applicant - available from Sep quarter 2011)".
value_definition: A single character, Y or N, attached to a person within a VA_CASE_ID. One case has one primary applicant and any number of secondary applicants.
limitation: Primary applicant is an administrative role, not a household head and not the higher earner. Secondary applicants on skilled visas often hold qualifications and work histories that this file simply does not record, so reading the flag as a skill ranking will mistake a missing measurement for a real difference.
rationale: ABS names the primary and secondary applicant distinction as a Home Affairs visa data item in its overseas migration methodology, which is the same administrative role this flag records.
evidence_quote: Visa applicant type (primary or secondary applicant - available from Sep quarter 2011)
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's sentence about a flag indicating primary or secondary applicants and the generic no-value-list line twice, so it never connected the flag to the sparsity of the skills columns or warned it is not a skill ranking.

value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24
variable_description: The code naming which departmental processing system handled the application. Home Affairs has run visa processing across several long-lived systems, and column suffixes elsewhere in this table name two of them: ICSE on the sponsorship and stream columns, TRIPS on the grant table. ABS names TRIPS as the department's Travel and Immigration Processing System when describing the administrative data it takes from Home Affairs. Because the system decides which columns are populated, this is a data quality field before it is an administrative fact.
value_definition: A short code identifying the system of record for the application. The value set is small and reflects departmental IT history rather than anything about the applicant.
limitation: It cannot be read as a visa type even though it correlates with one, because paper-lodged and online-lodged cases of the same subclass have gone to different systems in the same year. A shift in the mix of source systems over time will also move the completeness of other columns with no change in the underlying migration.
rationale: The ABS overseas migration methodology names the department's Travel and Immigration Processing System and confirms that these administrative data are collected by Home Affairs under the Migration Regulations, which is the system landscape this code indexes.
evidence_quote: Aside from persons travelling as Australian or New Zealand citizens, persons travelling to Australia are required to provide information in visa applications. These administrative data are collected by the Department of Home Affairs under the authority of the Migration Regulations 1994 made under the Migration Act 1958.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only that it identifies the application source system, with the generic no-value-list sentence used as both value definition and limitation, so it never named a system or explained that the source system predicts which other columns are filled.

value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, Migrant settlement outcomes methodology, 2025
variable_description: The visa stream in words, the level below subclass that says which pathway within a subclass an application used. A single subclass often holds several streams, so a partner visa and a skills visa each split into pathways the subclass number alone will not show. It aligns with VA_TYPE_LONG_DS and VA_TYPE_L2_LONG_DS, and the ICSE suffix on the custodian's note marks the system it comes from.

The labels are also unstable over twenty-five years, and a series grouped on the text will break where a stream was renamed or split.
rationale: The ABS methodology sets out how visa streams are formed for statistical purposes, which is the comparison a reader of this column needs in order not to confuse the department's stream with the ABS one.

value_domain: Visa grant number carried on the application
value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, PLIDA data and legislation
variable_description: The grant number recorded on the application, which is how an application is tied to the visa it produced. It is populated only where the application resulted in a grant, so it is the join between the application and grant sides of this collection and the counterpart of TR_VISA_GRANT_NUMBER. Its presence is the closest thing the application table has to an outcome field.
value_definition: A grant identifier attached to a person on an application. Each person granted a visa on a case carries their own number, so it identifies a person's grant rather than the case.
limitation: A blank cannot be read as a refusal. Applications on hand at the extract, withdrawn applications and refused applications look identical here, so a grant rate computed from the presence of this column is too low by however many cases were still being decided at the extract date.
rationale: The ABS PLIDA page confirms the Home Affairs feed carries both visa applications and visa grants, which is the pairing this number implements.
evidence_quote: Information on visa types, start & end dates, & data on educational studies for student visas & working arrangements for skilled migration visas.
supersedes_rationale: The entry printed the custodian's phrase about the visa grant number for the visa applicant, with the generic no-value-list line as both value definition and limitation, so it never said what a blank means or that this is the join to the grant table.

variable_description: The visa programme in words, the top of the departmental visa hierarchy, such as the Migration Program or the Temporary Visa Program. It is the broadest grouping in this table, sitting above report group, subclass, type and stream. Programme is the level at which government sets planning levels, so it is the right level for asking how many people entered under a capped permanent programme against an uncapped temporary one.
value_definition: Long text naming a departmental visa programme. The vocabulary is small, of the order of a handful of values, and sits above every other visa descriptor in the table.
limitation: The programme says where the visa came from, not where the person ended up. Temporary programme entrants who later gain permanent residence appear under both programmes across their history, so summing programmes across years counts the same person more than once and overstates permanent migration if the transitions are not removed.
rationale: The ABS methodology sets out the aggregation of visa subclasses into the highest level groupings used for migration statistics, which is the level this column names in the department's own vocabulary.

It is the level most published departmental migration statistics use, and it is close to but not the same as the ABS visa streams, which are built from the bottom: "Visa subclass (3-digit) information was aggregated into visa streams (highest-level grouping)". Reading this column gives the department's grouping without having to aggregate subclasses yourself.

value_domain: Home Affairs visa subclass code on the application

variable_description: The subclass code of the visa applied for, the finest level of the visa hierarchy in this table, for example 489 or 601. Subclasses are prescribed under the Migration Regulations 1994, the authority ABS names for this material: "These administrative data are collected by the Department of Home Affairs under the authority of the Migration Regulations 1994 made under the Migration Act 1958." On this table the code describes what was sought; TR_VISA_SUBCLASS_CD on the grant table describes what was given, and the two can differ where a case was decided into a different subclass.
value_definition: A three digit code identifying a visa subclass. New subclasses are created and old ones closed as the migration programme changes, so the set present depends on the application year rather than being fixed across the file.
limitation: An unfamiliar code is not automatically an error, because it may be a subclass closed years before the extract, and a closed subclass will pass any numeric range check. Check a code against the subclass list in force for its application year before treating it as a visa or as a fault. The code also records what was sought, so a series built on it counts demand for a subclass rather than entry on one.
rationale: The ABS methodology states that visa application information is collected by Home Affairs under the Migration Regulations 1994, which is the instrument that prescribes the subclasses this code names.
evidence_quote: Aside from persons travelling as Australian or New Zealand citizens, persons travelling to Australia are required to provide information in visa applications. These administrative data are collected by the Department of Home Affairs under the authority of the Migration Regulations 1994 made under the Migration Act 1958.

value_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, Migrant settlement outcomes methodology, 2025
variable_description: The visa subclass written out, the number and its name together, such as 601 Electronic Travel Authority. It is the readable form of VISA_SUBCLASS_CD and the safest column for reading a single case, because the name says what the visa is where a bare number does not. Group on the code rather than the text: subclass names have been changed without the code changing, so grouping on words splits one subclass into several.

Two people on the same named subclass can hold different work, study and stay conditions, and a subclass whose name mentions skills does not confirm the person was assessed on skills, because secondary applicants carry the same name as the primary applicant.
rationale: The ABS methodology confirms that the three digit subclass is the base unit from which visa groupings are built, which is what this label names in readable form.
